data.narrative:
Proxima Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised €200M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms operating in frontier nuclear technology, including Valar Atomics, Helion, Fuse Energy, X-Energy, and Oklo.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the €200M raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $400M. Peer-median analysis references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics (Series B, $6.0B), Nano Nuclear Energy (Seed, $808M), and Fuse Energy (Series A, $200M)—producing a median valuation of $808M. The peer range spans $200M to $6.0B, reflecting stage and technology dispersion across the nuclear frontier sector.

The two methods triangulate to a range of $340M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $604M. This implies a valuation roughly 1.5x to 4.6x the capital raised. Key uncertainties include stage-specific capital efficiency assumptions and the wide dispersion within the peer set, which reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity, commercialization timeline, and regulatory pathway across fusion and advanced fission subsectors.
